en: to be reliable; to be trustworthy

examples.ko: 새로 온 후배는 말이 적지만 믿음직해 보여요.
examples.en: The new junior colleague says little but looks reliable.

examples.ko: 동생이 이삿짐을 번쩍 드는 모습이 믿음직했어요.
examples.en: It was reassuring to see my younger brother lift the moving boxes with ease.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 믿음직한 사람이라서 다들 따라요.
examples.en: Our team leader is trustworthy, so everyone follows them.
My father's broad shoulders felt dependable.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 오래된 곳이라 더 믿음직해요.
examples.en: This shop has been around a long time, so it feels more trustworthy.
My son has become a dependable young man before I knew it.

explain: '믿음직스럽다'로도 말하고 뜻은 거의 같아요. 보는 사람이 '맡겨도 되겠다'고 느끼는 모습이나 태도를 칭찬할 때 써요. 명사 앞에서는 '-ㄴ'을 붙여 '믿음직한 사람'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: My older brother is reliable, so I don't worry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '믿음직하다'와 뜻이 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as '믿음직하다'.

phrases.en: Minsu is a really reliable friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '믿음직한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, use the form '믿음직한'.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 약속을 자주 잊어서 믿음직하지 않아요.
phrases.en: He often forgets promises, so he isn't reliable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿을 수 없다는 느낌을 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to say someone is not trustworthy.

explain_en: General word for being reliable, keeps promises (믿음직한 친구) You can also say '믿음직스럽다' with almost the same meaning. It praises someone's look or attitude that makes the viewer feel they can be trusted with things. Before a noun, use '-ㄴ', as in '믿음직한 사람'.

t90.ax: My father's broad shoulders felt dependable.

examples.en: The same mistake keeps repeating.
It feels like the days repeat exactly the same.
If the work repeats, it gets boring.
I'll be careful so the same thing doesn't happen again.
Today repeated the same thing as yesterday.
Thanks to repeated practice, I became good at it.

explain: 같은 일이 다시 일어날 때 써요. 내가 하면 '반복하다', 저절로 되풀이되면 '반복되다'예요. 순우리말로는 '되풀이되다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: This problem keeps repeating, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계속'을 붙이면 같은 일이 여러 번 일어난다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '계속' stresses that the same thing happens many times.

phrases.en: They say history repeats itself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반복되다'와 뜻이 같고 순우리말이라 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '반복되다', but a native Korean word that sounds softer.

phrases.en: I'm careful so that the same thing doesn't happen again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않게'와 함께 다시 일어나지 않기를 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-지 않게', it expresses hope that something won't happen again.

explain_en: Routine or pattern happening again and again, neutral (일이 반복되다) Use it when the same thing happens again. If you do it, it is '반복하다'; if it just recurs, '반복되다'. A native Korean equivalent is '되풀이되다'.

examples.en: Korea has a well-developed subway system.
Children develop in body and mind while playing.
I want to work in a country with advanced technology.
If you exercise, your muscles will develop more.
As the internet developed, shopping became easy.
The tourism industry is well developed in this area.

explain: '발달하다'가 '스스로 발전하다'라면 '발달되다'는 '발달된 상태'를 강조해요. '발달돼 있다', '발달된 기술'처럼 쓰는 일이 많아요. 사람이나 도시가 '좋아지고 커지는' 쪽의 변화에 써요.

phrases.en: A baby's brain develops quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 자라고 좋아지는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for change that grows and improves by itself.

phrases.en: Thanks to advanced technology, life has become easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 잘 발전한 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies the noun after it to mean well-developed.

phrases.en: The child's language development is fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '발달'을 써서 정도를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 발달 in a pairing that describes the degree.

explain_en: Passive state: skills, body parts or areas have grown naturally. 발달하다 is closer to 'grows by itself', while 발달되다 stresses the developed state. It often shows up as '발달돼 있다' or '발달된 기술'. It describes people, cities or fields growing and getting better.

dis.h: grow or mature naturally, like skills
gh: progress to a better, more advanced state

p.n: 발전되다 stresses moving forward to a better level.

t90.ax: Korea has a well-developed subway system.

en: to be explained; to be accounted for

examples.ko: 이 규칙은 책에 자세히 설명돼 있어요.
examples.en: This rule is explained in detail in the book.
The cause of the accident hasn't been explained yet.

examples.ko: 그 문제는 다음 시간에 설명될 거예요.
examples.en: That problem will be explained next class.

examples.ko: 어려운 말이 쉽게 설명되면 이해하기 편해요.
examples.en: When hard words are explained simply, they're easier to understand.
I tried it following the method that was explained.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 사전에 두 가지로 설명돼요.
examples.en: This word is explained in two ways in the dictionary.

explain: '설명하다'는 내가 알려 주는 것이고, '설명되다'는 글이나 자료에 풀이되어 있는 상태예요. 'A로 설명된다'는 학술적인 글에서 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '설명이 안 돼요'처럼 '설명이 되다'로 풀어서 말하는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: I can't explain why that happens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '설명되지 않아요' 대신 이렇게 풀어서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, people often say it this way instead of '설명되지 않아요'.

phrases.en: I studied the content explained in the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '풀이되어 있는'이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun, adding the sense of 'explained in'.

phrases.example: 이 현상은 날씨로 설명될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This phenomenon can be explained by the weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원인을 이유로 풀이할 때 글에서 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pattern often used in writing to explain something by its cause.

explain_en: Passive; something is made clear or accounted for. '설명하다' is you explaining; '설명되다' is something being laid out in a text or material. 'A로 설명된다' is common in academic writing. In speech people often split it as '설명이 되다', as in '설명이 안 돼요'.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹고 바로 누우면 소화가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you lie down right after eating, you don't digest well.
This food is digested slowly.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 게 아직 소화되지 않았어요.
examples.en: What I ate yesterday still hasn't digested.

examples.ko: 우유는 소화되기 어렵다고 말하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say milk is hard to digest.
Porridge is food that digests easily in the stomach.
If your food has settled, let's go for a walk.

explain: 음식이 주어이면 '소화되다', 먹는 사람이 주어이면 '소화하다'를 써요. 배가 불편할 때는 '소화가 안 돼요'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Porridge is easy to digest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 편하게 소화될 때 '소화가 잘 되다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say '소화가 잘 되다' when food digests comfortably.

phrases.en: Cold food doesn't digest well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 주어이고 소화가 어려울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with food as the subject when it is hard to digest.

phrases.en: I can't digest milk well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 사람이 주어이면 '소화하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '소화하다' when the person eating is the subject.

explain_en: Use 소화되다 when the food is the subject and 소화하다 when the eater is the subject. When your stomach feels bad, you can say 소화가 안 돼요.

examples.en: The army advances slowly.
The ship moved forward carefully through the fog.
Don't be afraid of moving forward.
You'll be able to move ahead as planned.

examples.ko: 포기하지 않고 계속 전진하면 길이 보여요.
examples.en: If you keep moving forward without giving up, the path will appear.
The robot is moving forward one step at a time.

explain: 전진하다는 앞으로 나아가는 거예요. 반대말은 '후진하다'예요. 사람이나 탈것이 앞으로 가는 것뿐 아니라 일이나 목표를 향해 나아가는 것에도 써요.

phrases.en: The soldiers keep advancing without rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멈추지 않고 계속 앞으로 나아간다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to keep moving forward without stopping.

phrases.en: We keep moving toward our goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 목표를 향해 노력하는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for working steadily toward a dream or goal.

phrases.en: The car doesn't move forward on the snowy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 나아가지 못하는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something cannot move forward.

explain_en: Advance forward, as troops or teams. 전진하다 is to move forward. Its opposite is '후진하다'. It covers people or vehicles going ahead, and also making headway toward a goal.

en: the use of chopsticks; chopstick skills

examples.en: I'm still clumsy with chopsticks.

examples.ko: 저는 젓가락질이 서툴러서 식당에서 포크를 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I'm not good with chopsticks, so I asked for a fork at the restaurant.
My foreign friend learned how to use chopsticks quickly.

examples.ko: 젓가락질 연습을 하려고 콩을 집어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried picking up beans to practice using chopsticks.
Using chopsticks is hard for everyone at first.

examples.ko: 젓가락질 하나만 봐도 밥 먹는 습관이 보여요.
examples.en: You can see someone's eating habits just from how they use chopsticks.

explain: '젓가락'은 도구이고 '젓가락질'은 그걸 쓰는 동작이에요. '젓가락질을 하다', '젓가락질이 서툴다/능숙하다'처럼 말하고, '가위질'처럼 도구 뒤에 '-질'이 붙은 말과 같은 방식이에요.

phrases.en: I learned how to use chopsticks from my grandmother when I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젓가락 쓰는 법을 익힌다는 뜻으로, '젓가락질을 하다'보다 배우는 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It talks about the process of learning, while 'to use chopsticks' just describes the action.

phrases.en: My friend is a foreigner, but she is skilled with chopsticks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서툴다'의 반대로, 젓가락을 잘 쓰는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 'clumsy'; used to praise someone who handles chopsticks well.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is good with chopsticks and can even pick up beans.
phrases.nuance_ko: '능숙하다'보다 더 편하게 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual way to say someone is skilled with chopsticks.

explain_en: '젓가락' is the tool, and '젓가락질' is the act of using it. You say '젓가락질을 하다' or '젓가락질이 서툴다/능숙하다', and it works like '가위질', where '-질' is attached to a tool.

examples.en: The author created a new story.
I played a song I composed myself for my friend.
Creating pictures or poems is enjoyable.

examples.ko: 이 이야기는 실제가 아니라 창작해서 쓴 거예요.
examples.en: This story isn't real; I made it up and wrote it.
The children are creating a dance on their own.
To create, you first have to read a lot.

explain: 이미 있는 것을 따라 할 때는 '모방하다'나 '따라 하다'를 쓰고, 새로 지어낼 때는 '창작하다'를 써요. 소설·노래·춤·시처럼 예술 작품과 잘 어울려요. 만든 사람은 '창작자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I want to create songs someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 새로 만들고 싶은 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 싶다' expresses a wish to create something new.

phrases.example: 방학 동안 창작 활동을 많이 했어요.
phrases.en: I did a lot of creative work during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글, 그림, 노래 등을 새로 만드는 일 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the overall work of making new writing, art, or music.

phrases.en: That creator is famous for webtoons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품을 새로 만든 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the person who made an original work.

explain_en: Making art such as a novel, song or poem. For copying something that exists, use '모방하다' or '따라 하다'; for inventing something new, use '창작하다'. It fits artistic works such as novels, songs, dances, and poems. The maker is called '창작자'.

p.n: 창조하다 sounds grander and stresses something wholly new; 창작하다 stresses writing or composing a work.

t90.ax: The author created a new story.

examples.en: In autumn, cosmos flowers bloomed fully along the road.
I took photos in a field of cosmos.
Cosmos blooms pink or white flowers.
I picked a cosmos flower on a country road.
A butterfly landed on the cosmos.
I like delicate flowers like cosmos.

explain: 가을에 피는 꽃으로 잘 알려져 있어요. '코스모스가 피다', '코스모스가 흔들리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The cosmos flowers sway in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '코스모스'와 같은 뜻이지만 '꽃'을 붙이면 피어 있는 꽃의 모습을 더 떠올리게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 코스모스, but adding 꽃 brings the blooming flower to mind.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the cosmos path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 코스모스가 줄지어 핀 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A road lined with blooming cosmos.

phrases.en: I went to the cosmos festival in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 코스모스를 보는 가을 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An autumn event for viewing cosmos flowers.

explain_en: It is a flower well known for blooming in autumn. People say it blooms or sways.

examples.en: I study Korean a little every day.
Yesterday I studied new words with an app.
Studying alone can be boring at times.

examples.ko: 제가 학습하는 방법을 조금 바꿔 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried changing the way I study a little.
I'm studying grammar with this book.
I review what I studied every day.

explain: 말할 때는 '공부해요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '학습'은 교재·교육 자료·인공지능 설명 같은 글에서 자주 보여요. '학습 자료', '학습 계획'처럼 명사로 붙여 쓰는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: I study Korean every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 일상 말로, 말할 때는 '학습하다'보다 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word with the same meaning, used much more than 학습하다 in speech.

phrases.example: 이 앱에는 좋은 학습 자료가 많아요.
phrases.en: This app has many good study materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교재나 공부할 때 쓰는 자료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for textbooks and other materials for studying.

phrases.en: I made a study plan for this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부할 계획을 말하는 글이나 말에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in writing or speech about a plan for studying.

explain_en: Formal, written word for learning or studying. In speech '공부해요' sounds far more natural. 학습 shows up in textbooks, teaching materials and explanations of AI. It is often attached as a noun, as in '학습 자료' (study material) and '학습 계획' (study plan).

dis.h: formal, written word for learning or studying

p.n: Same meaning; 공부 sounds more everyday.

t90.ax: I study Korean a little every day.

examples.ko: 비가 오고 나면 흙냄새가 진하게 나요.
examples.en: After it rains, there's a strong smell of earth.

examples.ko: 흙냄새를 맡으니까 어릴 때 생각이 났어요.
examples.en: Smelling the earth reminded me of my childhood.

examples.ko: 이 흙냄새는 비 오기 전에 항상 나요.
examples.en: This earthy smell always comes before rain.
The smell of soil in the garden lifted my mood.

examples.ko: 새 운동화에 흙냄새가 배어서 빨아야 해요.
examples.en: My new sneakers have soaked up a dirt smell, so I need to wash them.

examples.ko: 아이들은 흙냄새 나는 운동장에서 신나게 뛰어놀았어요.
examples.en: The kids ran around happily on the earthy-smelling field.

explain: 발음이 [흥냄새]로 바뀌는 점에 주의하세요. 비 온 뒤나 시골, 텃밭 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 보통 좋은 느낌으로 말해요.

phrases.en: I like the earthy smell after rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흙냄새가 가장 잘 떠오르는 장면이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The scene where the smell of earth comes to mind most.

phrases.en: I like the earthy smell now that I'm in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 느낌을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to express a pleasant feeling.

phrases.en: Smelling the soil in the garden calms me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새를 느낀다는 뜻으로, '맡다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '맡다' to mean smelling it.

explain_en: Note that it is pronounced [흥냄새]. It often comes up when talking about after the rain, the countryside or a garden, and usually has a pleasant feel.
